Brief: Tell me about the Aral Sea and the efforts to restore it. — about Impact on environment, economy, and public health

1. The Aral Sea is considered an example of ecosystem collapse.
2. The ecosystems of the Aral Sea and the river deltas feeding into it have been nearly destroyed, largely because of the salinity being dramatically higher than ocean water.
3. The receding sea has left huge plains covered with salt and toxic chemicals from weapons testing, industrial projects, and runoff of pesticides and fertilizer.
4. Because of the shrinking water source and worsening water and soil quality, pesticides were increasingly used from the 1960s to raise cotton yield, which further polluted the water with toxins (e.g. HCH, TCCD, DDT).
5. Industrial pollution also resulted in PCB and heavy-metal contamination.
6. Owing to the insufficiency of water left in the Aral Sea, concentrations of these pollutants rose drastically both in the remaining water and in the dry beds.
7. This resulted in wind-borne toxic dust that spread quite widely.
8. People living in the lower parts of the river basins and former shore zones ingested pollutants through drinking local water and inhaling contaminated dust.
9. Furthermore, due to absorption by plants and livestock, toxins—many of which bioaccumulate and are not easily broken down or excreted by the liver and kidneys—entered the food chain.
10. Inhabitants of the surrounding areas commonly experience a shortage of fresh water, and health problems are widespread—including high rates of certain cancers, respiratory illnesses including tuberculosis (mostly drug resistant), digestive disorders, anaemia, and infectious diseases.
11. Liver, kidney, and eye problems may also be due to the toxic dust storms.
12. The dust storms have also contributed to water shortages through salt deposition.
